主要内容: The document titled '40-F' is an annual report filed by Magna International Inc. with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on March 29, 2018. The report covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2017. Magna International Inc. is a Canadian company incorporated in the Province of Ontario. The report includes audited annual financial statements and an Annual Information Form. The company has 358,325,403 outstanding common shares. The filing indicates that the company is not an emerging growth company as defined under Rule 12b-2 of the Exchange Act. The report also confirms that the company has filed all required reports under Section 13 or 15(d) of the Exchange Act during the preceding 12 months and has been subject to such filing requirements for the past 90 days. The document outlines the financial reporting requirements for a U.S. registrant under SEC filings. It includes the Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2017, and references the Annual Report to Shareholders for the same period. The registrant has filed its audited annual financial statements and management discussion and analysis with the SEC. The document also addresses forward-looking statements and disclosure controls and procedures. The registrant has not elected to use the extended transition period for complying with new or revised financial accounting standards. The information provided is not part of the annual report on Form 40-F and is not filed with the Commission. The document outlines the corporate governance practices of Magna International Inc., a foreign private issuer listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). It details the composition of the Audit Committee, which includes Lawrence D. Worrall (Chair), Peter G. Bowie, Dr. Kurt J. Lauk, and William A. Ruh. The company has designated these members as 'audit committee financial experts' and confirmed their independence and financial literacy. The document also includes the company's code of ethics, which applies to all employees, including senior executives. Additionally, it provides information on the fees paid to the principal accountant, Deloitte LLP, for services rendered during the fiscal years ended December 31, 2017, and December 31, 2016. The fees are categorized into audit, audit-related, tax, and other services, with audit fees comprising the majority of the total. The company has also disclosed significant differences in its corporate governance practices compared to U.S. domestic issuers, as required by NYSE listing standards.
